macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Ripple Secures MiCA CASP Authorization Across 30 EEA Countries
items.summary: Ripple reportedly received full MiCA CASP authorization from Luxembourg’s CSSF, expanding its ability to offer regulated crypto payments across the European Economic Area. The license adds to Ripple’s growing set of regulatory approvals and is one of the clearest major regulatory developments in the latest crypto news cycle.

items.title: EU Prepares to Reopen MiCA Rules for Non-EU Stablecoin Issuers
items.summary: EU diplomats told Euronews that the European Union is considering reopening the MiCA rulebook in 2027 to address stablecoin issuers outside the bloc. The move would mark a significant follow-up regulatory step after MiCA’s initial rollout.

items.title: ESMA Launches Crypto Custody Review After MiCA Deadline
items.summary: Analytics Insight reports that ESMA has begun a sweeping review of crypto custody practices following the MiCA deadline. This suggests continued regulatory scrutiny of how client assets are safeguarded in Europe.

items.title: Bitcoin Supply in Loss Hits Record 10.8 Million BTC
items.summary: Crypto.com says the amount of Bitcoin trading below cost basis has reached a record 10.8 million BTC. That signals broad market stress and is a notable market-development headline, though it is not a direct price quote.

items.title: MegaETH TVL Drops 59% in 24 Hours After Aave V3 Withdrawals
items.summary: KuCoin’s news feed says MegaETH’s total cross-chain TVL fell sharply in the past 24 hours, with Aave V3 withdrawals blamed for much of the decline. The move highlights rapid liquidity shifts across newer DeFi ecosystems.

items.title: Bonzo Lend Loses $9 Million in Hedera Oracle Exploit
items.summary: Cointelegraph reports that Bonzo Lend suffered a $9 million loss in an oracle exploit on Hedera. The incident is one of the largest security events in the latest batch of crypto headlines.

items.title: Summer.fi Reports $6 Million Flash-Loan Vault Exploit
items.summary: CoinMarketCap Academy says Summer.fi lost about $6 million after an attacker used a large flash loan to manipulate vault accounting and drain funds into DAI. The exploit adds to a strong run of DeFi security incidents.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam Reaches Final Development Phase
items.summary: Crypto.com reports that Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade has entered its final development phase. The milestone is a notable project-development update for the network’s next major protocol work.

items.title: Vitalik Buterin Outlines Multi-Year ‘Lean Ethereum’ Rebuild
items.summary: CoinMarketCap Academy says Vitalik Buterin described a 3- to 4-year overhaul aimed at quantum safety, privacy, cheaper data storage, and possibly replacing the EVM. If implemented, it would represent one of Ethereum’s most ambitious roadmap shifts in years.

items.title: Solana Activates First Formal On-Chain Governance System
items.summary: CoinMarketCap Academy reports that Solana has activated on-chain governance, allowing validators with 100,000 SOL staked to submit proposals. The change is a significant protocol-development step for the network.

items.title: XRP Ledger Tokenized Assets Reach $4 Billion
items.summary: Analytics Insight says tokenized assets on the XRP Ledger have reached $4 billion. The figure underscores growing real-world-asset and tokenization activity on the network.

items.title: Kraken Seeks European Banking License
items.summary: Analytics Insight reports that Kraken is pursuing a European banking license as part of its regulatory expansion. That would further blur the line between crypto exchange services and traditional financial infrastructure if approved.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, extending its push into professional AI tools. The launch intensifies competition in the enterprise AI market.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice model
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The models are rolling out across multiple ChatGPT tiers.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning the model for broader use by developers. The move puts additional pressure on competing AI providers charging for model access.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI introduced Grok 4.5, describing it as its most capable model yet for coding and agentic workflows. The release underscores continued rapid model iteration among frontier AI companies.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, the oversight body intended to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The appointment highlights governance and oversight as a growing theme in advanced AI development.

items.title: OpenAI faces renewed copyright scrutiny in New York lawsuit
items.summary: A newspaper group led by The New York Times asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about its ability to search internal systems for evidence in a copyright dispute. The case adds to broader legal pressure on AI training practices.

items.title: Meta announces major Alberta data center buildout
items.summary: Meta said it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand computing capacity for AI workloads. The announcement reflects the broader industry trend toward aggressive infrastructure investment.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy’s data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for violations of data protection rules. The action adds to regulatory scrutiny of AI chatbot platforms in Europe.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 ports released on PS4 and PS5
items.summary: IGN reports that Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 are now available on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5, though the release comes at a high cost to players.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced sets a new franchise peak on Steam
items.summary: IGN says Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced reached around 100,000 concurrent players on Steam, making it the series’ biggest player peak on the platform so far.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown after 7 years
items.summary: IGN reports that Nintendo will shut down Mario Kart Tour this September after seven years of service, and no offline version will be offered.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass subscriber growth reportedly falls short of Microsoft’s targets
items.summary: IGN reports that Xbox leadership has acknowledged Game Pass has not grown as Microsoft expected, with reports saying it is tens of millions of subscribers short of earlier targets.

items.title: GTA Online’s next update, The Kortz Center Heist, gets a release window
items.summary: IGN says Rockstar’s next GTA Online update is The Kortz Center Heist, due next week, and fans have already spotted Rockstar-related Easter eggs in the lead-up.

items.title: PlayStation physical disc plans draw backlash after reports of a 2028 shift
items.summary: The Verge reports that Sony is moving toward ending physical PlayStation game discs for new games released after January 2028, sparking strong reactions across the gaming community.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly sells off four Xbox studios amid major gaming cuts
items.summary: The Verge reports that Microsoft is divesting Double Fine, Compulsion Games, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs as part of a significant restructuring of its gaming business.

items.title: Mortal Shell 2 gets a release date
items.summary: Overworld reports that Mortal Shell 2 will launch on August 20, 2026 for PS5, while other coverage notes pre-orders are live and the game is priced at £45/$50.

items.title: Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis shutdown date announced
items.summary: Overworld reports that Final Fantasy VII Ever Crisis will shut down on October 6.

items.title: Crimson Desert announced for Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: GameMAG reports that Crimson Desert will release on Nintendo Switch 2, adding a notable third-party title to the new console’s lineup.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: India removes import duty on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on several parts used to make mobile phones and other electronic devices, a move that could lower costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi. Reuters said the change eliminates the existing 7.5% and 5% levies on selected components.

items.title: Apple broadens chip-supply deal with Broadcom
items.summary: Apple plans to spend more than $30 billion under a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom that also includes an expansion of a Colorado factory. The deal underscores Apple’s push to secure more domestic chip supply.

items.title: Meta plans first AI chip manufacturing run in September
items.summary: Meta is planning to start manufacturing its own AI chip from September, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters. The company is aiming to boost its overall computing capacity to 14 gigawatts next year.

items.title: EU lawmakers back interim rules for child abuse content detection
items.summary: EU lawmakers backed a proposal to reinstate temporary rules allowing platforms such as Google and Meta to detect and remove online child sexual abuse material. The measure would preserve moderation tools while longer-term rules are worked out.

items.title: Coinbase restores prediction markets trading after outage
items.summary: Coinbase said it restored prediction markets trading after a technical issue interrupted access. The incident highlights continued reliability pressures on major crypto and fintech platforms.

items.title: Australia raises big tech fee to fund local news
items.summary: Australia increased its levy on major technology platforms to help fund local news outlets. The policy adds new regulatory and cost pressure on large internet companies operating in the country.

items.title: Meta announces first data center in Canada
items.summary: Techmeme reports that Meta will build its first Canadian data center, a 1GW facility in Alberta projected to cost about $9 billion and take two to three years to complete. The project is part of Meta’s broader infrastructure expansion.

items.title: EU court dismisses Apple challenge to DMA gatekeeper designation
items.summary: Techmeme reports that the EU General Court dismissed Apple’s legal challenge to its designation as a Digital Markets Act gatekeeper for the App Store and iOS. The ruling reinforces the EU’s regulatory authority over large platform operators.
